To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stick-slip propensity of a given brake pad material can be measured by means of the frictional response, the system natural frequencies and the system damping ratio.

a) the frictional response can be characterized using the friction coefficient, the frictional hysteresis and the stick-slip propensity; b) the stick-slip is a dynamic phenomenon that can be characterized in terms of frictional hystesis and frictional stiffness; and c) the stick-sip propensity is related to the material composition and the surface texture of the pad material.

the propensity of a brake pad to generate groan noise emission can be assessed by measuring the stick-slip propensity of the pad material when sliding on a counterface under controlled boundary conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experimental evaluation of the propensity of brake pads to generate stick-sip vibrations and groan noise emissions.
the development of a new methodology, based on the measurement of the frictional response, to evaluate the propensity of the pad material to stick-slip.
the frictional response, the stick-slip propensity and the noise emission of brake pad materials.

a pad material with higher propensity to stick-slip is more likely to generate groan noise emission, when used in a brake system.
the stick-slip propensity of the tested materials can be ranked as: Kevlar>Graphite>Sintered Metal.
the friction coefficient of the pad material is the key parameter to control in order to reduce the propensity of the brake pad to generate stick-slipping vibrations.

the proposed methodology allows for the experimental evaluation of the propensity of a brake pad lining to stick-slip, which is in line with the groan noise emission.
the frictional response is a key parameter in the propensity to generate groan noise, and that the frictional behavior of the pad material is strongly dependent on its composition.
the stick-slip instability is more likely when the frictional response is highly dependent on the sliding speed and the contact is not lubricated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stick-slip propensity of a brake pad material is strongly dependent on the surface topography of the disc counterface.
the stick-slip propensity of a brake pad material can be evaluated in a laboratory environment, under controlled conditions, using a simple and robust methodology.
a simple experimental methodology can be applied to compare the propensity of brake pad materials to stick slip and groan noise emission.
